newsitem.title: CHINA: Hainan Air says in damage dispute.
newsitem.headline: Hainan Air says in damage dispute.

text.p: China's Hainan Airlines Co Ltd said on Wednesday it was seeking compensation of about $2.25 million from an aircraft maintenance company for damage to one of its planes during routine repairs.
The Chinese airline linked to financier George Soros said one of its leased Boeing 737s was damaged when it slipped off a hoist during repairs by another state-owned company last month.
"We are still discussing compensation with the maintenance company," said a Hainan Airlines spokeswoman.
The airline had already received $750,000 in compensation for the damage but was seeking additional payments, partly to cover other expenses and lost revenues.
The maintenance was being conducted in Chengdu city in southwestern China by Southwestern Aircraft Maintenance Co.
Boeing had since sent a team to oversee repairs that were now nearly complete, the airline spokeswoman said.
Hainan Airlines has B shares for foreign investors listed on the Shanghai stock exchange.
American Aviation, an investment company partially owned by Soros, has about 21 percent of the airline's registered capital.
